$comment: Packages whose risk no scanner reports: young, single-maintainer, low-download, abandoned, or shipping unreadable artifacts. Enforced by strape/scripts/high-scrutiny-check.mjs — any version or integrity change fails CI and forces a re-read. reviewedAt/reviewedBy stay null until a human signs off; the Claude Code dep-review pass produced the capability notes, not the sign-off.

grok-mermaid.reason: Created 2026-07-28, single maintainer, ~1.2k downloads/month, and a direct production dependency of the CLI. Statically imported by the interactive TUI (packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/mermaid.ts), so the runtime module denylist cannot cover it without breaking interactive mode.
grok-mermaid.escalation: If a full read raises any doubt: vendor into strape/vendor/grok-mermaid with a root overrides file: entry (costs one lockfile regeneration), or drop mermaid rendering from the TUI.

proper-lockfile.reason: Unpublished since 2022-06-24 — abandoned upstream despite ~84M downloads/month. An abandoned package with a live npm publish right is a standing account-takeover risk, and it performs filesystem locking on paths strape cares about (session/auth files).
proper-lockfile.escalation: Node's fs primitives plus an atomic temp+rename would replace it; consider vendoring if the account is ever flagged.

@silvia-odwyer/photon-node.reason: Single maintainer, and ships WASM — the payload cannot be meaningfully read. Used for image processing of attachments. Review basis is provenance + capability scan + pinning, not a source read.
@silvia-odwyer/photon-node.escalation: If image attachment support is not needed for the Grok/OpenAI workflow, removing the feature removes the dependency entirely.

@mariozechner/clipboard.reason: Loads a prebuilt native .node binary (10 platform-specific sibling packages, all in the shipped closure). Native code is unreadable in review; it is also the only native module left after the hunk-2 trim removed ssh2/cpu-features.
@mariozechner/clipboard.escalation: Platform packages are pinned by integrity hash; a changed hash on the same version means republication and must be treated as hostile.
